claims.text: The rider does not contest the dwell arithmetic, and this brief puts no weight on it. The driver's own trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 507 seconds from 06:41:10 to the cancellation at 06:49:37, against a free waiting period in force of 300 seconds on this STANDARD-class pickup, so the derived shortfall figure of minus 207 seconds is a surplus, not a deficit, and POL-NS-06's shortfall route is not this case's route. The rider's case is the separate question POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09 decide, namely whether this driver may take money out of the fee at all.

The driver's own profile meets both limbs of the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check on the platform's numbers: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips in the same window, which is 11.5 per cent - above the 8 per cent rate limb and well above the absolute limb of 4. These are the only two profile fields POL-NS-07 reads, and they are cited here for that test alone, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Even taking the driver's account at its highest, with POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, that tripped check means his 80 per cent compensation is withheld outright and the case is escalated under POL-NS-09, limb (d) making a tripped anti-farming check a mandatory escalation. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues, the 4.00 cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded, and the escalation packet must carry a direction to the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full. That escalation, with the refund direction inside it, is the ruling the rider asks this tribunal to record; NO_ACTION is not the rider's claim, because on a rider-filed dispute it would leave the charge standing under POL-GEN-03.

The 4.00 is not yet in the platform's hands: the fare record shows a 4.00 cancellation-fee line with payment_status PENDING, total_charged 4.50 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Holding that state while the anti-farming pattern is reviewed is the outcome that keeps the rider from funding a charge the platform has not resolved, which is the express purpose POL-NS-07 gives the hold.

Every abuse trigger POL-NS-09 can read on the rider points the other way. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires, and rider and driver each show 0 disputes with the other in the last 90 days under limb (c). The rider's lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure is a different counter from no_show_disputes_30d, and POL-GEN-01 forbids reading the lifetime counter in the clause's place, so nothing in the rider's citable profile supports an adverse finding or a refusal of this escalation.

The contested amount is 4.00, below the 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05, so on any ruling that lets the fee stand the charge is executed automatically without a human reading this file. The POL-NS-07 hold, carried into a POL-NS-09 escalation, is the only mechanism on this record that stops a 4.00 fee being collected from the rider while the driver's 7 no-show terminations in 30 days are examined.

Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is met on the face of the record: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 06:41:20, and the trip was never boarded and was terminated by the driver rather than completed.

Limb (b) is met: the GPS trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius on 52 qualifying fixes, the first of them at 06:41:10 - ten seconds before the 06:41:20 arrival event - so the arrival geofence test of POL-NS-02 is satisfied on admissible, in-radius readings rather than on a single stray fix at the edge.

Limb (c) is met with 207 seconds to spare: the driver's own trace shows a single unbroken in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds, running from 06:41:10 to 06:49:37, against the free waiting period of 300 seconds in force for this STANDARD-zone trip. The run count is 1, so no accumulation across separate intervals is needed and POL-NS-06(i) is not in play.

Limb (d) is met: the trip record shows the driver terminated the trip at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - at or after the moment the required 300-second dwell had elapsed, since the dwell ran the full 507 seconds - and no boarding event is recorded anywhere on the trip.

The arrival marker is not false and POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock: the qualifying in-geofence run opens at 06:41:10, ten seconds BEFORE the 06:41:20 arrival event, so the driver was already inside the radius holding position when he marked arrival. Under POL-NS-05 limb (iii), even a marker that slightly preceded the arrival would not defeat a fee whose corrected dwell meets the minimum, and here there is nothing to correct.

This is not a wrong-entrance case and POL-NS-03 decides nothing: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m arrival radius - his closest recorded approach to the pickup pin is 14.5 m - and not in the 50 m to 400 m band that POL-NS-03 governs, so POL-NS-03 yields to POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a rider message that is locating or coordinating, and the chat log holds four messages - one from SYSTEM and three from the driver - with nothing at all from the rider, so the rider-contact route never opens. The driver separately placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered, which defeats the clause even where the chat shows nothing.

The rider's own device track is present and affirmatively places it roughly 1.9 km from the pickup point for the whole waiting window - 118 fixes, minimum recorded distance 1894 m, and zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is therefore failed on admissible evidence, not merely undecidable, and the rider's assertion that he 'did come down' is contradicted by his own GPS.

The rider never cancelled, so the grace provisions of POL-NS-10(a) to (c) cannot be reached on these facts: the trip record shows cancelled_by DRIVER at 06:49:37, some seventeen minutes after acceptance at 06:32:50. No limb of POL-NS-10 returns a driver-terminated no-show charge to the rider.

No traffic advisory covers Woodlands Ave 6 in this window: EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so it can carry no fact either way. That costs the driver nothing, because the 507-second dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required to clear the 300-second minimum.

On the merits the fee is chargeable and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee in force for this trip - SGD 3.20, the net figure the fare arithmetic itself returns and the figure the trip record's platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.00 supports.

I do not conceal the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check, and on this driver's own record both its limbs are met: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips, a rate of about 11.5 percent, above the 8 percent threshold. Compensation is therefore withheld and the case routes to human review under POL-NS-09(d) - a portfolio-level risk signal, not a finding about this trip. Because escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, the fee stands held and the rider's claim to the SGD 4.00 does not succeed on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The arrival and waiting facts favour the driver, but the driver's own profile sends the case to human review, so nothing is collected or refunded today.

RIDER — on the merits your refund claim does not succeed. EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius at Blk 682 from 06:41:10 to the cancellation at 06:49:37: one unbroken in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds against the free waiting period of 300 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a surplus of 207 seconds against EV-GPS-00207.derived.arrival.shortfall_sec of -207. His 06:41:20 arrival tap came ten seconds after he was already in the radius, and he was stationary (speed 0.0 kph), so POL-NS-05 finds no false arrival marker; no boarding event is recorded and he terminated under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW. Your statement that you 'did come down' is not supported: the rider_track in EV-GPS-00207 holds 118 fixes, none inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, the closest 1894 m from the pin, for the whole waiting window. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you — you sent no chat message (EV-CHAT-00207 holds one SYSTEM and three DRIVER entries) and the driver's 06:45:10 in-app call went unanswered. POL-NS-06 gives you nothing (507 s against the 300 s minimum) and POL-NS-10 does not apply (you did not cancel). POL-NS-03 does not apply either: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius (closest approach 14.5 m), not in the 50–400 m wrong-entrance band. POL-NS-01 is therefore satisfied on all four limbs and the SGD 4.00 fee would be chargeable.

DRIVER — what takes the case off the ordinary charge/refund route is your own record. Both limbs of the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check are met on the platform's numbers: EV-DPROF-00207 shows no_show_terminations_30d of 7 (the limb requires 4 or more) and 7 divided by 61 completed trips in the same 30 days is 11.5%, above the 8% rate limb. Under POL-NS-07 your compensation — 80% of the SGD 4.00 fee in force, SGD 3.20 (EV-FARE-00207.derived.money.driver_compensation) — is WITHHELD, and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). Escalation is terminal: no monetary outcome issues, and the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded. The fare record shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.50, payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and that state is preserved.

Open question for the human reviewer: whether the driver's 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days reflect genuine rider no-shows or fee-farming. Per POL-NS-07 the escalation packet must direct the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 in full if the pattern is not explained (see referrals).

The POL-NS-09 abuse triggers on the rider do not fire: EV-RPROF-00207.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (limb (d) needs 3 or more) and both parties show 0 disputes with the other in the last 90 days (limb (c)). The rider's lifetime prior_no_show_flags is a different counter and may not be read in place of no_show_disputes_30d.

Confidence 0.95. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact is at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-GPS-00207, EV-TRIP-00207, EV-DPROF-00207, EV-FARE-00207), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no deciding fact here: the 507-second dwell is a single run, so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required and the fee does not depend on it. Both the SGD 4.00 fee and the SGD 3.20 compensation are below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, but escalation holds them regardless.
referrals: POL-NS-07: the escalation packet must direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full — the driver's 80% compensation (SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00 fee) is withheld under the anti-farming check (7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips, 11.5%).

ruling.explanation:
The case is escalated to a human reviewer. No money moves now: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded while the review is pending.

To the driver. On the merits of this trip you were right on every limb of POL-NS-01, and both advocates agree on the arithmetic. The trip record carries your 'arrived' event at 06:41:20; the GPS trace places you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius on 52 qualifying fixes from 06:41:10, ten seconds before that event, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 (you were stationary, in-radius, at the marker time). You held one continuous in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds, ending at the 06:49:37 termination - 207 seconds more than the 300-second free-wait period in force on this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so there is no POL-NS-06 shortfall and no accumulation is needed. You terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW at or after that dwell elapsed, with no boarding, so limb (d) holds. POL-NS-03 does not apply: your stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius (closest approach 14.5 m), not in the 50-400 m wrong-entrance band. On that basis the SGD 4.00 fee was chargeable and your payout would be 80% of it, SGD 3.20.

But your own profile trips the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check, which reads only the two counters that clause names: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips, a rate of 11.5%, above the 8% limb and above the absolute limb of 4. POL-NS-07 therefore withholds the SGD 3.20 and sends the case to human review under POL-NS-09(d). That is a portfolio-level risk signal, not a finding that you did anything wrong on this trip.

To the rider. Your account that you 'came down, just a few minutes later' is not supported by the record. You sent nothing in the chat log - all four messages are from the driver or the system - so POL-NS-04 limb (a) never opens; and your own device track sits about 1.9 km from the pickup for the whole window (118 fixes, minimum recorded distance 1894 m, none inside the 100 m rider-presence radius), so limb (c) is affirmatively failed rather than undecidable. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you, and on this trip the SGD 4.00 was chargeable. POL-NS-10 is not reached: you did not cancel, the driver did.

What helps you is the driver's own anti-farming pattern. Because it trips, the case escalates, the SGD 4.00 stays held rather than being collected - the fare record shows payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - and the escalation packet carries POL-NS-07's direction to the reviewer to refund your fee in full. Escalation is not itself a refund, and it is not a rider win: the reviewer decides, and the fee remains frozen meanwhile. The contested SGD 4.00 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05, but a POL-NS-09 escalation displaces execution while review is pending.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0; it can carry no fact and nothing turns on it, because the 507-second dwell is a single unbroken run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required. The facts that decide the escalation rest on artifacts at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, driver profile), so no discount applies under POL-GEN-02(2).

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this case cannot be finished by an automated ruling, so the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is held — not collected from the rider, and not refunded to him — until a human reviewer decides it. Here is why, and what the reviewer must settle.

On the facts, the driver's no-show charge is made out under POL-NS-01. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00207) carries an 'arrived' event at 06:41:20, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00207) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius on 52 qualifying fixes, the first at 06:41:10, and shows a single unbroken in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds against the 300-second free waiting period read from the record's platform_policy.free_wait_sec. That is a surplus of 207 seconds, so POL-NS-06's shortfall route does not help the rider, and because the dwell is one continuous run no traffic advisory is needed for POL-NS-06(i) — the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no deciding fact. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: the driver was already stationary in the radius ten seconds before it. POL-NS-03 does not apply either — his closest approach to the pin was 14.5 m, inside the arrival radius rather than in the 50–400 m wrong-entrance band.

The rider-side routes do not open. POL-NS-04 limb (a) needs a locating or coordinating message from the rider; the chat log (EV-CHAT-00207) holds four messages and none is his. His own device track in EV-GPS-00207 places it about 1.9 km from the pickup for the whole window on 118 fixes, none inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, so limb (c) is not merely undecidable but affirmatively failed, and his account that he 'did come down' is contradicted by his own GPS. POL-NS-10 does not apply because the rider did not cancel.

What stops the case is the driver's own profile (EV-DPROF-00207). POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips on both limbs: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips is at least 4 and 11.5 per cent, above the 8 per cent rate limb. Compensation is therefore withheld — the 80 per cent figure of SGD 3.20 on the SGD 4.00 fee is not paid — and POL-NS-09(d) makes the case escalate to human review. ruling.explanation:
Driver and rider: this case produces no money ruling today — it goes to a human reviewer.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00207) carries a driver 'arrived' event at 06:41:20 and a driver termination at 06:49:37 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00207) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius on 52 qualifying fixes, the first at 06:41:10, and shows one unbroken in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds running 06:41:10 to 06:49:37, against the free waiting period of 300 seconds in force for this trip (EV-TRIP-00207 platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 300). All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are therefore met: (a) the arrived event, (b) in-geofence fixes falling before it, (c) a 507-second dwell against a 300-second minimum, and (d) RIDER_NO_SHOW recorded at or after the dwell elapsed. Nothing displaces that result. POL-NS-03 does not apply — the driver's closest recorded approach to the pin is 14.5 m, inside the radius, not in the 50–400 m band. POL-NS-04 does not apply — the chat log (EV-CHAT-00207) holds four messages, none from the rider, the driver placed an unanswered in-app call at 06:45:10, and the rider's own device track sits about 1,900 m from the pickup with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-05 does not apply — the arrival marker was not false, because the driver was already inside the radius at 06:41:10, ten seconds before he tapped. POL-NS-06 does not apply — there is no shortfall; the dwell is a surplus, not a deficit. POL-NS-10 does not apply — the rider never cancelled. On the merits alone, POL-NS-07 would fix the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee in force, i.e. SGD 3.20.

WHY THERE IS NO MONEY RULING. POL-NS-07 makes that payout subject to an anti-farming check read from EV-DPROF-00207, and the check trips on both its limbs: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days (limb: 4 or more) against 61 completed trips in the same window, a rate of 11.5 percent (limb: above 8 percent). Those are the only two profile fields the clause reads. Where the check trips, POL-NS-07 withholds the compensation and mandates escalation under POL-NS-09(d), which is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues, and the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is HELD rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. Both money fields are therefore null. This is not a finding that this no-show was not genuine — the evidence shows it was — but a portfolio-level risk signal about the driver's recent termination pattern, which the human reviewer settles.

DIRECTION TO THE REVIEWER. POL-NS-07 requires the escalation packet to direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full; that direction is carried in the referrals above, so the rider's SGD 4.00 is not collected meanwhile.

ON THE SURVIVING CLAIMS. The driver's four limb-by-limb claims on POL-NS-01, and the driver's points on POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-10, are accepted. The driver's own concession that the POL-NS-07 check trips is accepted, and it is the fact that decides the case. The driver's framing that the rider's claim 'does not succeed' is accepted only so far as the escalation holds the amount: on a POL-NS-09 escalation the fee is neither kept nor returned, and it is not a ruling against the rider. The rider's points that the abuse triggers do not point at the rider are accepted (no_show_disputes_30d = 1, below the 3 limb (d) requires; 0 cross-disputes in 90 days) — they simply do not touch the driver-side trigger. The rider's POL-GEN-05 point (contested amount SGD 4.00, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold) is moot: an ESCALATE ruling has no monetary effect to execute. The rider's payment-status point is accepted as context: EV-FARE-00207 shows the 4.00 line with payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, which is the state the hold preserves.

DISCARDED CLAIM. One claim was discarded by the referee before I read it — the driver's advisory claim, which relied on the MISSING, weight-0.0 EV-ADVIS-00207-01 without naming its issue code (IMPAIRMENT_UNDISCLOSED). The substance it made — that POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unnecessary on a single 507-second run — survives anyway, because the reasoning above rests on EV-GPS-00207 and EV-TRIP-00207 and never needed the absent advisory.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying the facts above — EV-GPS-00207, EV-TRIP-00207, EV-DPROF-00207 and EV-FARE-00207 — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. I set confidence at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; the escalation here is triggered by POL-NS-09(d), not by any doubt about the facts. This ruling is provisional and either party may appeal it under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The rider does not contest the dwell arithmetic, and this brief puts no weight on it. The driver's own trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 507 seconds from 06:41:10 to the cancellation at 06:49:37, against a free waiting period in force of 300 seconds on this STANDARD-class pickup, so the derived shortfall figure of minus 207 seconds is a surplus, not a deficit, and POL-NS-06's shortfall route is not this case's route. The rider's case is the separate question POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09 decide, namely whether this driver may take money out of the fee at all.

The driver's own profile meets both limbs of the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check on the platform's numbers: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips in the same window, which is 11.5 per cent - above the 8 per cent rate limb and well above the absolute limb of 4. These are the only two profile fields POL-NS-07 reads, and they are cited here for that test alone, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Even taking the driver's account at its highest, with POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, that tripped check means his 80 per cent compensation is withheld outright and the case is escalated under POL-NS-09, limb (d) making a tripped anti-farming check a mandatory escalation. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues, the 4.00 cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded, and the escalation packet must carry a direction to the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full. That escalation, with the refund direction inside it, is the ruling the rider asks this tribunal to record; NO_ACTION is not the rider's claim, because on a rider-filed dispute it would leave the charge standing under POL-GEN-03.

The 4.00 is not yet in the platform's hands: the fare record shows a 4.00 cancellation-fee line with payment_status PENDING, total_charged 4.50 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Holding that state while the anti-farming pattern is reviewed is the outcome that keeps the rider from funding a charge the platform has not resolved, which is the express purpose POL-NS-07 gives the hold.

Every abuse trigger POL-NS-09 can read on the rider points the other way. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires, and rider and driver each show 0 disputes with the other in the last 90 days under limb (c). The rider's lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure is a different counter from no_show_disputes_30d, and POL-GEN-01 forbids reading the lifetime counter in the clause's place, so nothing in the rider's citable profile supports an adverse finding or a refusal of this escalation.

ledger.claim: The contested amount is 4.00, below the 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05, so on any ruling that lets the fee stand the charge is executed automatically without a human reading this file. The POL-NS-07 hold, carried into a POL-NS-09 escalation, is the only mechanism on this record that stops a 4.00 fee being collected from the rider while the driver's 7 no-show terminations in 30 days are examined.

Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is met on the face of the record: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 06:41:20, and the trip was never boarded and was terminated by the driver rather than completed.

Limb (b) is met: the GPS trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius on 52 qualifying fixes, the first of them at 06:41:10 - ten seconds before the 06:41:20 arrival event - so the arrival geofence test of POL-NS-02 is satisfied on admissible, in-radius readings rather than on a single stray fix at the edge.

Limb (c) is met with 207 seconds to spare: the driver's own trace shows a single unbroken in-geofence dwell of 507 seconds, running from 06:41:10 to 06:49:37, against the free waiting period of 300 seconds in force for this STANDARD-zone trip. The run count is 1, so no accumulation across separate intervals is needed and POL-NS-06(i) is not in play.

Limb (d) is met: the trip record shows the driver terminated the trip at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - at or after the moment the required 300-second dwell had elapsed, since the dwell ran the full 507 seconds - and no boarding event is recorded anywhere on the trip.

The arrival marker is not false and POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock: the qualifying in-geofence run opens at 06:41:10, ten seconds BEFORE the 06:41:20 arrival event, so the driver was already inside the radius holding position when he marked arrival. Under POL-NS-05 limb (iii), even a marker that slightly preceded the arrival would not defeat a fee whose corrected dwell meets the minimum, and here there is nothing to correct.

This is not a wrong-entrance case and POL-NS-03 decides nothing: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m arrival radius - his closest recorded approach to the pickup pin is 14.5 m - and not in the 50 m to 400 m band that POL-NS-03 governs, so POL-NS-03 yields to POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a rider message that is locating or coordinating, and the chat log holds four messages - one from SYSTEM and three from the driver - with nothing at all from the rider, so the rider-contact route never opens. The driver separately placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered, which defeats the clause even where the chat shows nothing.

The rider's own device track is present and affirmatively places it roughly 1.9 km from the pickup point for the whole waiting window - 118 fixes, minimum recorded distance 1894 m, and zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is therefore failed on admissible evidence, not merely undecidable, and the rider's assertion that he 'did come down' is contradicted by his own GPS.

The rider never cancelled, so the grace provisions of POL-NS-10(a) to (c) cannot be reached on these facts: the trip record shows cancelled_by DRIVER at 06:49:37, some seventeen minutes after acceptance at 06:32:50. No limb of POL-NS-10 returns a driver-terminated no-show charge to the rider.

No traffic advisory covers Woodlands Ave 6 in this window: EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so it can carry no fact either way. That costs the driver nothing, because the 507-second dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required to clear the 300-second minimum.

ledger.claim: On the merits the fee is chargeable and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee in force for this trip - SGD 3.20, the net figure the fare arithmetic itself returns and the figure the trip record's platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.00 supports.

I do not conceal the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check, and on this driver's own record both its limbs are met: 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips, a rate of about 11.5 percent, above the 8 percent threshold. Compensation is therefore withheld and the case routes to human review under POL-NS-09(d) - a portfolio-level risk signal, not a finding about this trip. Because escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, the fee stands held and the rider's claim to the SGD 4.00 does not succeed on this record.
